content:
If sentiment is positive and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1–2% in early horizon to avoid overconfidence.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending down, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid horizon to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast deviates >3% from recent 7-day average, apply a 1–3% correction toward historical mean.  
In late horizon, if sentiment is mixed and forecast is volatile, dampen slope by 15–25% to prevent overfitting.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days and forecast is flat, shift forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days and forecast is flat, shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bearish drift.
